purpose: Retrospective separate-sequence check of the prompt-region conditioning deletion effects observed in seq11. Seq9 and seq10 were not used to train the exploratory channel gate, but they were already used in earlier validation and inspected; they are not independent test data or proof of generalization.
frames: Use the existing frozen five-target selection per sequence from split_preflight_attempt03, retaining only targets at least seven frames after the automatic initial prompt so comparable histories exist. This yields seq9 frames 17,28,39,50 and seq10 frames 22,24; selection uses frame indices, not target labels. Seq3 frames 8 and 12 are engineering gates only.
capture: Replay the previously captured automatic raw-window sequence without changing prompt, model, memory, geometry or propagation. Add the existing read-only attention/decoder snapshot observer inside the verified feature capture. Check all video masks, memory traces, recorded features and prompt provenance against the archived feature-capture run; compare seq3 engineering snapshots with previously verified raw snapshots. Repeat engineering gate in two fresh processes.
experiment: Apply exactly the previously fixed condition-region deletion protocol, 1024 of 4096 conditioning tokens per arm, with foreground, background, boundary, spatial uniform, shuffled and offline full-attention-usage control. Keep all other keys and pointers intact. All reduced arms share identical attention-key count; the no-op is an unequal-key reference. No target labels are used for selection or replay.
evaluation: Require reproducible fresh-process predictions, independent rank/position and mask audits, and open labels only after replay outputs are frozen. Report frame-level Dice, present-frame means and labeled-empty false alarms. The attention-ranked arm requires the full original read and is not deployable. No conclusions about patient independence or full-video performance. No new detector calls, inference thresholds or gates.
